claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch based on aggregate readiness and monitoring-oriented public guidance despite an unresolved 1.4-point evaluation gap in the tax filing assistant segment and without confirmed disclosure resolution or approved risk acceptance for that named launch use case.
decision_criteria: Verdict is compliant only if admissible evidence shows the named-segment weakness was either resolved, disclosed as required, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and monitoring guidance can support operational prudence, but they do not satisfy the internal disclosure predicate on their own.
When legal review is pending and the affected segment is named in partner commitments, product characterizations such as non-core or low-volume are insufficient to defeat materiality.
evidence_requests: Provide final legal disposition of the open disclosure ticket.
Provide evidence that the tax filing assistant limitation was disclosed in the model card or launch materials before launch.
Provide approved pre-launch risk acceptance explicitly covering this named launch use case and the 1.4-point gap.
Provide contractual or launch-scope evidence showing the two tax-season partner commitments do not make this a named launch use case or contractual customer segment.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence shows the tax filing assistant segment misses target and is named in two tax-season partner commitments, which makes materiality more likely under the policy text.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no such disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a key policy predicate remains unresolved.
The product note calling the segment non-core because it is 6% of projected traffic does not resolve materiality under the stated policy when named commitments and pending legal review exist.
Public governance guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring deployment does not override the internal release policy requirement for disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the current record despite the unresolved named-segment gap.
That omission of a material weakness disclosure is adequately supported by admissible evidence.
That aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are sufficient to satisfy the disclosure policy for the named launch use case.
That the affected segment can be treated as immaterial based on low projected traffic despite named partner commitments and open legal review.
